_comment: PERFORMANCE suite: the MySQL connector at a scale where one ingested table has more than 100K rows -- container-connectors/mysql.json's surface, read from a seeded airportdb domain instead of world. Functions in functions/perf_mysql_airportdb.py (caps_datagen.py and _srcmeta.py are copies of container-connectors/functions'). Run: `tdd xp one-shot --suite performance/mysql_airportdb`. SCALE: the source domain loads size 1000 (`create-data --size 1000`, ~131K rows, ~5 MB): booking has exactly 100,000 rows, so the base reads it twice with UNION ALL — one 200,000-row booking table, no join — to cross 100K; size 10000 would give 1M bookings but ~2.2M rows (weather grows 100x) to seed. SOURCE (`mysql_in`, reads mysql_airportdb_l): base (booking UNION ALL booking — the 200K-row ingest — plus flight and airline), _inc (booking_id watermark, LIMIT 10 — re-run to walk), _none (WHERE 1=0), _multiquery (2 slim queries, transactional=False). DEST (`mysql_out`, input from dev datagen `caps_input/cap_rows`): _append (create then accumulate) and _replace (create then DROP+recreate) on distinct tables cap_append/cap_replace; re-run to observe. schema_evolution (strict by default, or update) is exercised by the schema-evolution suites. Domains: dev (datagen), mysql_airportdb_l (source), mysql (dest). SRC METADATA: mysql_meta_keep and mysql_meta_drop (mysql_in) read the same one-query SELECT over airline (aliased to the code/name columns functions/_srcmeta.py asserts) with and without the `tabsdata.src_metadata.drop` src_cfg key, and one transformer each in collection mysql_meta (group ops) asserts that side, as in container-connectors/mysql.json.
